answer: The page ends up with the icon from the first tag in its `tags` list that sets one. If the page sets its own `pageDecoration` (in its frontmatter or via a `transform`), that wins over any tag's.

## A page carries several tags that each define a page icon through tag.define. Which icon does it end up with, and what if the page sets its own?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Page Decorations.md] ---
### Apply to every page with a tag

# Apply to every page with a tag
To decorate every page with a tag, give the tag a `pageDecoration` in [[API/tag|tag.define]] in your [[CONFIG]]:

```lua
tag.define {
  name = "person",
  pageDecoration = { icon = "user", cssClasses = { "person-page" } },
}
```

A page’s own `pageDecoration` (from its frontmatter, or a `transform`) wins over the tag’s. When several of a page’s tags set the same field, the first tag in its `tags` wins. `cssClasses` from all of them are combined. Changing a tag’s decoration re-indexes the pages with that tag, so there is no need to run `Space: Reindex`.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/API/icon.md] ---
### icon.feather

## icon.feather
`icon.feather(name)`

Renders a Feather icon to SVG markup by name, or nil when the name isn’t a Feather icon. The markup carries no color of its own (`currentColor`) and a default 24x24 size, both of which CSS at the injection site can override.

**Parameters:**

- `name` (`string`) — A Feather icon name, e.g. `trash-2`.

**Returns:**

- `string` — The icon’s SVG markup, or nil when unknown.

**Example:**

```lua
local lock = icon.feather("lock")
```

--- [vault:corpus/docs/API/icon.md] ---
### icon.resolveFeather

## icon.resolveFeather
`icon.resolveFeather(names)`

Renders a batch of Feather icons to SVG markup in one round trip, so panels can show icons without bundling the icon set themselves. Unknown names are omitted from the result. The markup carries no color of its own (`currentColor`) and a default 24x24 size, both of which CSS at the injection site can override.

**Parameters:**

- `names` (`table`) — Feather icon names, e.g. `trash-2`.

**Returns:**

- `table` — Map of icon name to SVG markup.
<!--/lua-->

Use `icon.feather` for a single name in hand right away — widget HTML, a custom panel’s content. `icon.resolveFeather` batches several names in one round trip, which is what [[API/view|view]] icons use internally — don’t call either for those, though: name them in the view instead (`icon = "lock"`, or `icon = "feather:lock"`) and the view resolves them, lazily and in one batch per view refresh. See [[API/widget#Presentation]].

[Feathericons.com](https://feathericons.com) lists the available names. The namespace is the point, not the implementation: `icon.feather`/`icon.resolveFeather` are the first of what could eventually be more than one icon set, each reached the same way (`icon.<set>...`) if and when a second one arrives — `icon.lucide`, say.

### API > tag.define(spec)

## tag.define(spec)
Defines a tag explicitly.

`spec` is a table that can contain:
* `name` (required) the name of the tag
* `tagPage` page to navigate to when clicking the tag (defaults to `tag:name`)
* `metatable` to set a custom Lua metatable for objects with this tag.
* `mustValidate` a boolean defining whether or not schema validation must pass for the object to be indexed
* `schema` [[Schema]] to validate against
* `icon` a [Feather](https://feathericons.com) icon name for the tag itself, shown in the [[Workbench]]. Unlike `pageDecoration`, it doesn't decorate the tag's pages; when it's absent, `pageDecoration.icon` is used.
* `pageDecoration` [[Page Decorations|page decoration]] (`icon`, `prefix`, `cssClasses`, …) for every page with this tag. See [[Page Decorations#Apply to every page with a tag]].
* `validate` callback function invoked when an objects needs to be validated, returns `nil` or an error message.
* `transform` callback function invoked when an object with tag `name` has been indexed. Allows you to make changes to it, skip indexing altogether or generate additional objects.
* `renderFrontmatter` callback function `function(pageMeta, ctx)` that renders the [[Frontmatter]] of pages with this tag as a custom widget in the editor. See [[#Frontmatter live previews]].
* `renderDataBlock` callback function `function(object, ctx)` that renders each object of a ` ```#name ` [[Tag/data|data block]] as a custom widget in the editor. See [[#Data block previews]].

### Use cases > Rendering objects > Frontmatter live previews

### Frontmatter live previews
When multiple tags in a page’s `tags` field define `renderFrontmatter`, the first one wins. Pages without such a tag fall back to the renderer of the `page` tag, which every page carries. The `page` tag’s renderer is the default form. The `liveEdit.frontmatter` setting (**Edit frontmatter as a form** in the [[Workbench/Configuration|Configuration tab]]) turns it off, and so does `tag.define { name = "page", renderFrontmatter = config.unset }`. Without any renderer, frontmatter shows as plain YAML. A tag’s own `renderFrontmatter` applies either way.
